channel.title: Found & Sent - A Postcard Archive
channel.description: Rescued vintage postcards with their original messages, stamps, and stories. New cards added regularly.

item.title: Card #146: Seattle, Washington — Space Needle (June 20, 1969)
item.description: From: Lee & Helen | To: Lash Florists, 604 Richland Ave, Wheeling, WV 26003 | Franklin D. Roosevelt 6¢ stamp, postmarked 6/20/69. Photo by Max R. Jensen. Published by C.P. Johnston Company, Seattle, WA. Color by Mike Roberts, Berkeley, CA. Card C23803. Aerial view of the Space Needle with Lake Union below. Message written mid-flight at 37,000 feet over South Dakota: "The Tighes are really 'up in the air' — 37,000 feet! Traveling at 570 miles an hr. over So. Dakota. Just crossed the wide Missouri. Jet flying beats the old T.W.A. When you can see below the clouds, it looks like a big map. In Space Needle last night."

item.title: Card #147: Fairbanks, Alaska — Aerial View (August 2, 1974)
item.description: From: Mable | To: Col. and Mrs. Herb Blizzard (U.S.A.F. Ret.), 29 Village Drive, The Fairways, Somers Point, NJ 08244 | Eisenhower 8¢ stamp, postmarked AUG 2 1974. Photo by Frank Whaley. Mirro-Krome card by H.S. Crocker Co., San Bruno, CA. Published by Arctic Circle Enterprises, Fairbanks, AK. Aerial view of Fairbanks with the Chena River winding through the city; fall foliage visible. Message: "Hi — On last leg of 5-wk. bus tour of Alaska. Hate to see it end. 37 of us aboard. Have seen some lovely country — plus many beautiful snow-capped mountains — glaciers, lakes etc. 8,467 miles all together. Just Great. Love, Mable."

item.title: Card #148: Bremen, Germany — Town Musicians Sculpture (c. 1979)
item.description: From: Unknown (family, hometown sender) | To: Nancy Lee, Box 42, Depoe Bay, OR 97341, USA | 80 Pfennig Deutsche Bundespost truck/industry stamp (c. late 1970s–early 1980s). Airmail (Mit Luftpost / Par Avion). Photo by Gerd Luers, Bremen. Published by Papeterie Einkaufsgesellschaft mbH, 2800 Bremen. Front shows the iconic Bremer Stadtmusikanten bronze sculpture — donkey, dog, cat, and rooster stacked in a tower. Message: "Hi, greetings from my hometown. We are having a wonderful time, so busy doing many things. The weather is indescribably hot. The girls speak beautiful German. We have been all over Germany. Was great together with Bill, we miss him. They Mom & Dad say hello. See you soon. Love from us all."
